sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description:
Retrieves and extracts the main content of a web page as markdown.

Include a 'prompt' parameter to have an LLM distill the page down to just the information you need — this saves significant context compared to ingesting raw page content.
Without a prompt, the full extracted markdown is returned (or a structured overview if the page is large).

Batch mode: use 'pages' instead of 'url' to fetch multiple URLs in a single call. Each entry can have its own prompt.
This is much faster than making separate web_fetch calls when you need content from several pages.
The 'url' and 'pages' parameters are mutually exclusive. Maximum 10 pages per batch.

When to use something else:
- The gh CLI (via bash) for anything on GitHub — issues, PRs, repo contents, API calls.

Behavior notes:
- URLs must include the scheme (e.g. https://). Plain HTTP is silently upgraded to HTTPS.
- Fetched content is held in a short-lived cache, so asking multiple questions about the same page is cheap.
- Cross-host redirects are surfaced rather than followed — make a second request to the target URL.
- No files or external state are modified by this tool.

url.description: Fully-formed URL to fetch (e.g., https://example.com/page). Mutually exclusive with 'pages'.

prompt.description: What information to extract from the page. Strongly recommended — the page content will be processed by a fast LLM and only relevant information returned. Omit only if you need the full raw content. Only used with 'url', not 'pages'.
What information to extract from this page

pages.description: Array of pages to fetch concurrently (max 10). Mutually exclusive with 'url'. Each entry can have its own prompt.

# Agent Instructions

## Development Philosophy

Treat documentation and tests as first-class deliverables, not supporting material. A working application is only complete when the docs and tests explain what was built, why it behaves that way, and how to verify or regenerate it.

This project may be iterated from a clean slate. Code can be removed, rewritten, or replaced as the design improves. The persistent memory is the combination of:

- modular documentation,
- automated tests,
- manual test plans,
- fixtures and expected outputs,
- architecture and product decision records.

A future coding agent with no prior memory should be able to rebuild the application, or any meaningful part of it, from those artifacts.

## Context Discipline

Coding agents have limited context windows. Keep project knowledge modular and task-oriented.

Before working, load only the documents directly relevant to the task. For example:

- UI work should read UI architecture, layout, design, and interaction docs.
- Backend work should read API, storage, workflow, and runtime docs.
- Agent workflow work should read pipeline, tool, evaluation, and ablation docs.
- Test work should read fixture, scoring, and expected behavior docs.

Do not force future agents to read a giant handoff document to understand a small subsystem. If a decision matters to one subsystem, put it in that subsystem's document. If it cuts across the whole project, put it in a short shared principles or architecture document and link to it.

## Reuse Without Context Bloat

Before implementing fresh code, styles, types, fixtures, helpers, or docs, check the relevant shared surfaces for the domain you are touching. Prefer reusing existing libraries, utilities, tokens, mixins, schemas, fixtures, or documented patterns over creating parallel implementations.

Use the narrowest search scope that is likely to be useful:

- the local file or component,
- the domain's shared primitives,
- one clearly similar neighboring implementation when helpful.

Do not scan unrelated subsystems by default. Broad duplicate-pattern searches should be explicit refactor tasks, not a prerequisite for ordinary feature work.

If you notice duplicated local behavior or styling while working, either promote it to the appropriate shared layer when the abstraction is obvious and low-risk, or leave a short note for a focused reuse/pattern-promotion refactor.

## Documentation Standards

When implementation changes durable behavior, update the relevant docs in the same iteration. Durable behavior includes:

- product behavior,
- user experience,
- architecture boundaries,
- data contracts,
- API contracts,
- security and privacy rules,
- agent workflow stages,
- configuration switches,
- failure behavior,
- test expectations.

Prefer small, named documents with clear ownership over long mixed-purpose documents. Keep documents comprehensive enough to regenerate behavior, but scoped enough that an agent can load only what it needs.

## Work Tracking

Use Gitea issues for actionable work and repository Markdown docs for durable project memory. The issue workflow, label vocabulary, epic convention, and docs-vs-issues split are described in [docs/authoritative/engineering/work-tracking.md](docs/authoritative/engineering/work-tracking.md).

## Testing Standards

Tests are part of the specification. Add or update tests when behavior changes.

Use tests to capture:

- expected success paths,
- failure and recovery behavior,
- important edge cases,
- regression fixtures,
- output contracts,
- safety and privacy constraints,
- known bugs that must not return.

When a feature cannot be fully automated yet, add a manual test plan with clear steps and expected results.

## Verification Before Review

After each meaningful commit and before marking work ready for review, run the deterministic checks for every domain touched by the change. Start from the modular verification index at [docs/authoritative/engineering/verification/README.md](docs/authoritative/engineering/verification/README.md), then load only the domain-specific verification documents that apply to the files you changed.

Verification requirements are domain-owned because frontend, Tauri shell, backend, workflow, documentation, and model-assisted checks have different runtimes and failure modes. If a required command cannot run in the current environment, document the exact command, the exact blocker, and any narrower checks that did run.

## Ablation and Iteration

Design important workflows so they can be tested in different configurations. Prefer explicit switches over hidden behavior.

For agentic or model-assisted systems, make it possible to compare:

- deterministic vs. model-assisted paths,
- different model prompts or providers,
- enabled vs. disabled validation stages,
- enabled vs. disabled external context,
- different retry, repair, and verification policies.

Persist the configuration used for each run so results are explainable and reproducible.

## Working Rule

For every meaningful change, ask:

1. Does the code work?
2. Do the tests prove the behavior we care about?
3. Do the docs preserve enough context to rebuild this later?
4. Is the knowledge placed in a modular location a future agent can find without loading the whole repository?

The change is not finished until all four answers are yes, or any exception is explicitly documented.

# Question Clarification

## Theoretical Grounding

The first analysis stage is grounded in CRISP-DM's Business Understanding phase. Before translating a user request into analysis tasks, the system must understand the business objective, assess the situation, determine the analytic goal, and identify the information needed for a useful plan.

Use Goal-Question-Metric as the operational pattern inside this stage:

```text
Goal -> questions that resolve the goal -> data or metrics needed to answer those questions
```

This stage exists because a technically valid analysis can still answer the wrong question. A user request like "What caused customers to cancel?" is not ready for interpretation until the system has checked whether the user supplied enough goal, scope, outcome, time, and decision context to produce useful analysis.

Reference sources:

- CRISP-DM 1.0 Step-by-step data mining guide, especially the Business Understanding phase: https://1library.net/document/qv7dvm1q-crisp-dm-step-by-step-data-mining-guide.html
- Goal-Question-Metric overview and original Basili framing: https://sebokwiki.org/wiki/Software_Modeling_and_Measurement%3A_The_Goal/Question/Metric_Paradigm

## Stage Contract

Question clarification runs after deterministic ingest and profiling, and before question interpretation. It receives:

- raw user question,
- uploaded or registered data summary,
- deterministic dataset profile,
- optional user-provided business context,
- privacy and external-search preferences if already known.

It produces a `QuestionClarificationSpec`:

```json
{
  "raw_question": "What caused customers to cancel?",
  "framework": "crisp_dm_business_understanding_with_gqm",
  "analysis_goal": "Understand likely drivers or risk factors for customer cancellation.",
  "known_inputs": {
    "dataset_available": true,
    "candidate_outcome_columns": ["canceled"],
    "candidate_time_columns": ["signup_date", "last_active_date"]
  },
  "unanswered_questions": [
    {
      "id": "time_period",
      "question": "What cancellation period should I analyze?",
      "reason": "The period defines the population and prevents mixing old and recent churn patterns.",
      "blocking": true
    }
  ],
  "non_blocking_defaults": [
    {
      "field": "causal_standard",
      "default": "association_or_risk_factors",
      "reason": "No experiment, intervention, or causal identification design was provided."
    }
  ],
  "should_ask_user": true,
  "can_proceed_to_interpretation": false,
  "reasoning_summary": "The dataset appears analyzable, but the business scope and cancellation period are underspecified."
}
```

## Clarification Dimensions

The gate should check these dimensions before question interpretation:

- Decision goal: what the user will do with the answer.
- Outcome definition: what counts as the target event or result.
- Population and scope: which rows, segments, products, geographies, or cohorts are in scope.
- Time period: which dates define the reported event window.
- Observation window: which behaviors are allowed as predictors because they occurred before the outcome.
- Causal standard: whether the user needs causal proof, predictive signals, or descriptive associations.
- Comparison baseline: retained customers, prior period, another segment, or overall average.
- Metric definitions: business definitions needed to interpret columns or derived metrics.
- Constraints: privacy rules, excluded rows or columns, test accounts, permissions, or policy limits.
- Success criteria: ranked findings, report, chart set, model quality, confidence intervals, recommendations, or reproducible artifact bundle.

## Asking Rule

Ask the user only when a missing answer would likely produce a misleading, blocked, unsafe, or low-value result. Ask at most a few high-value questions at once, ordered by impact.

Good first-pass questions for the churn fixture:

- "What cancellation period should I analyze?"
- "What counts as cancellation in this dataset: the `canceled` column, subscription end date, inactivity, or something else?"
- "Do you need evidence of true causation, or is a ranked list of associated risk factors acceptable?"

If the user does not answer and a safe fallback exists, record the fallback explicitly and continue only when the fallback is sufficient for a useful first pass. For example, association-oriented language is a safe default when no causal design is specified; an unstated cancellation period is usually not safe because it changes the population being analyzed.

## Relationship To Later Stages

Question clarification does not choose final predictor columns, build the DAG, search the web, or write the report. It decides whether the request is sufficiently specified for interpretation and records unresolved assumptions.

Question interpretation consumes either:

- a complete `QuestionClarificationSpec`, or
- the user's answers to the blocking clarification questions.

## Temporary Data Selection For The Current Slice

The implemented question workflow slice still builds a deterministic, temporary dataset profile in the TypeScript frontend before starting a question-clarification run. Browser-run development and browser UI tests use the HTML File API path so Vite remains the default automated workflow. The Tauri desktop runtime uses the shell-owned `pick_csv_file()` command to open a native picker for `.csv` and `.txt` files, return file name, size, path, and UTF-8 text, and then hand the text back to the same TypeScript profiling path.

This desktop picker is intentionally temporary. It proves native file selection for the CSV question flow, including visible failures for unsupported files or unreadable content, but it does not implement backend-owned ingest, durable project persistence, project-folder registration, or long-term data governance. The broader slice boundary and follow-up requirements live in [../architecture/vertical-slice-boundaries.md](../architecture/vertical-slice-boundaries.md).

In the implemented question workflow slice, the user's answers are appended to the run context ledger as a `clarification_answers` entry. The question-interpretation prompt receives the chronological ledger along with the original question, dataset profile, and accepted clarification spec. This lets later model calls understand user references such as "in my original question" or "when I clarified the last 6 months" from structured process history rather than fragile prompt concatenation.

Feasibility checks may still discover data-level blockers later, but predictable user-intent blockers should be moved into this stage.

# Local Backend

## Purpose

The local backend is the Python FastAPI sidecar that mediates between the desktop UI, local project files, local tool execution, and the remote OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint.

The first backend slice intentionally proves the model integration before the full DAG runtime, project store, or analysis tools are built.

## Current Package

```text
apps/backend/
  pyproject.toml
  src/insight_specialist_backend/
    config.py
    main.py
    model_client.py
    question_clarification_runs.py
    runs.py

```

## Runtime Configuration

The backend reads model endpoint settings from environment variables:

```env
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_BASE_URL=http://192.168.0.38:8000/v1
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_MODEL=insight-specialist-coder-local
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_API_KEY=dev-key
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=1024
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE=0
```

Defaults target a same-machine development server at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`. Remote development machines should override `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_BASE_URL` to the LAN address of the vLLM host.

## ModelClient Boundary

All LLM calls go through `insight_specialist_backend.model_client.ModelClient`.

The initial client supports:

- `GET /models`,
- `POST /chat/completions`,
- a deterministic smoke request that expects `local-backend-llm-ok`,
- sanitized endpoint reporting that does not expose the API key.

The client is intentionally implemented with the Python standard library for now so the LLM integration can be tested before the backend dependency stack is installed.

## FastAPI Surface

The current FastAPI app exposes:

```text
GET  /health
GET  /settings/model-endpoint
GET  /llm/models
POST /llm/chat
POST /llm/smoke-test
POST /stages/question-clarification
POST /runs/question-clarification
POST /runs/{run_id}/clarification-answers
GET  /runs/{run_id}
GET  /runs/{run_id}/events
```

`/settings/model-endpoint` must never return the raw API key.

`/llm/smoke-test` is the earliest integration test for the local model server. It makes a real chat completion request through `ModelClient` and returns `status: ok` only when the response content is exactly `local-backend-llm-ok`.

`/stages/question-clarification` is the first implemented workflow stage. It accepts a raw user question plus a deterministic dataset profile fixture, calls the configured LLM through `ModelClient`, parses strict JSON, validates the `QuestionClarificationSpec`, and returns the validated spec plus model metadata.

`/runs/question-clarification` is the first run-shaped vertical-slice endpoint. It starts the same question-clarification stage in a background thread and returns immediately with a `run_id`, `run_url`, and `events_url`. This endpoint is the preferred contract for the first frontend spike because it lets the UI show live progress while the model call is running.

`/runs/{run_id}` returns the current run snapshot, including status, event count, and terminal result or error when available. The initial implementation stores runs in memory; SQLite persistence comes later.

Run snapshots also include a chronological `context` array. This is the first in-memory version of the process context ledger. It is inspired by agent session logs in Codex, Claude Code, and pi: user, assistant/model, tool, and custom process entries are appended over time, and later prompts rebuild context from the ordered entries instead of depending on loose ad hoc variables.

The current ledger entries are domain-specific:

```text
analysis_request
question_clarification
clarification_answers
question_spec
```

Each entry records the run id, step, actor, entry type, timestamp, and structured content. Later SQLite persistence should preserve this append-only shape so a future agent can reconstruct how the user request became a technical analysis plan.

`/runs/{run_id}/clarification-answers` records user answers to blocking clarification questions, appends those answers to the context ledger, and starts the question-interpretation stage in a background thread. The endpoint returns the updated run snapshot plus `run_url` and `events_url`. The frontend should reopen the SSE stream with `?after=<last_seen_event_id>` after submitting answers.

The question-interpretation stage returns a `QuestionSpec`. `external_context_need_likelihood_1_to_100` is a planning signal for downstream internal analysis so date-bound or business-context findings can trigger better external-context questions later. It does not mean external search is required before internal analysis.

Backend stage schema modules use shared validation helpers from `insight_specialist_backend.schemas.validation` for required object, list, string, boolean, integer-range, and literal checks. New model-produced schemas should reuse this module so validation errors stay consistent across stages.

`/runs/{run_id}/events` is a Server-Sent Events stream. It replays existing events from the beginning by default, accepts `?after=<event_id>` or the `Last-Event-ID` header for resumption, emits heartbeat events while a run is still active and no new events are available, and closes after a terminal `succeeded` or `failed` status.

The backend installs CORS middleware for the local desktop/frontend boundary. It allows loopback browser origins such as `http://127.0.0.1:5173` and Tauri app origins, permits `GET`, `POST`, and `OPTIONS`, and allows the `content-type` and `last-event-id` headers needed by JSON writes and SSE resumption. Do not broaden this to arbitrary remote origins; the sidecar is a local unauthenticated API and should only be callable from the local app/development origins.

The current question-clarification event sequence is:

```text
run_created
run_started
stage_started
model_call_started
model_call_succeeded
stage_succeeded
run_succeeded
```

Failure runs emit `stage_failed` and `run_failed` instead of the success tail.

When clarification answers are submitted and interpretation succeeds, the run emits a second segment:

```text
clarification_answers_received
run_started
stage_started
model_call_started
```

# Chat and Clarification

## Role of Chat

Chat is an input and clarification surface. It is not the main representation of the work.

Chat is primary when:

- the user is asking the initial question,
- the user is uploading or describing data,
- the agent needs clarification,
- the user is changing scope,
- the user is asking about a completed result.

Chat should recede when:

- the analysis run has enough information to proceed,
- the user is monitoring progress,
- evidence and artifacts are being produced,
- the report is available.

Receding does not mean disappearing. The user should be able to reopen chat at any time to ask a status question, add context, or steer the analysis.

## Clarification Standard

The system should ask for help only when proceeding would likely produce a misleading, blocked, unsafe, or low-value result.

The first clarification pass is a CRISP-DM Business Understanding gate implemented with a Goal-Question-Metric pattern: clarify the user's goal, ask the smallest set of questions that materially affects the analysis, and identify the data or metrics needed before interpretation begins.

Good clarification questions:

- "What cancellation period should I analyze?"
- "Do you need causal proof, or is a ranked list of associated risk factors acceptable?"
- "Which column should be treated as the cancellation outcome?"
- "Should I use the uploaded lookup table as the source of region definitions?"
- "This file has two date columns. Which one defines the reporting period?"

Poor clarification questions:

- questions whose answer can be inferred from profiling,
- questions asked only to avoid making a documented default choice,
- questions that block the run even though a safe fallback exists.

## Non-Blocking Defaults

When a decision is not critical, the system should choose a default, record it, and continue.

Examples:

- Use HTML report output by default.
- Use deterministic profiling before model-assisted interpretation.
- Continue without external context when the context assessment says it is not needed.
- Use association language when the user asks casual causal questions and causal identification is not supported.

## Follow-Up During a Run

If the system needs the user during an active run, the request should be:

- rare,
- specific,
- visible in the dashboard,
- accompanied by a fallback if possible,
- framed around the consequence of answering or not answering.

The user should never have to read a long chat transcript to discover that the run is blocked.

## User-Initiated Chat During a Run

The user may think of something while the run is active:

- "I forgot to mention that the west region changed definition in March."
- "How much longer will this take?"
- "Can you also compare this by customer segment?"
- "Actually, ignore the test accounts."

The product should make this interaction natural. Reopening chat should not feel like interrupting a brittle background process.

There are three classes of user messages during a run:

- Status questions: answer from scheduler state, stage status, elapsed time, estimates, and logs.
- Additive context: attach the note to the run and apply it at the next safe planning or interpretation point.
- Steering changes: explain whether the change can be folded into the current run, requires a branch, or should launch a follow-up run.

## Deferred Chat Response

If the agentic system cannot answer immediately because a tool call, code execution, validation step, or report render is in progress, the UI should acknowledge the message immediately.

The acknowledgement should say:

- the message was received,
- whether the system is currently busy,
- when the user should expect a response,
- whether the message can affect the current run.

Examples:

```text
Got it. I am running the current validation step now and will respond when it finishes.
```

```text
I saved that note for this run. I will apply it before the interpretation and report-writing stages.
```

```text
I am in the middle of executing analysis code, so I cannot safely change the plan yet. I will check whether this can be folded in at the next checkpoint.
```

The user should see a visible pending state rather than wonder whether the system ignored them.

## Safe Steering Points

The runtime should define points where user steering can be incorporated safely:

- before autonomy handoff,
- after data profiling,
- after analysis planning,
- before code execution,
- after validation failure,
- before report generation,
- after report completion as a follow-up run.

When the user asks for a change outside a safe steering point, the product should queue the request and show where it will be considered.

Transport-wise, steering and follow-up messages should be writes, not event-stream payloads. The frontend should submit them through HTTP `POST` command endpoints. The backend should then emit SSE events that show whether the message was accepted, queued, applied at a safe point, or deferred.

## After Completion

After completion, chat can help the user ask follow-up questions about the report, request alternate views, or launch a new run. It should reference the report, evidence manifest, artifacts, and logs rather than relying on memory of the conversation.

import json
import threading
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Iterable, Literal


RunStatus = Literal["queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed"]
TERMINAL_STATUSES: set[RunStatus] = {"succeeded", "failed"}


class RunNotFoundError(KeyError):
    """Raised when a run id is not known to the current backend process."""


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunEvent:
    id: int
    run_id: str
    type: str
    timestamp: str
    payload: dict[str, Any]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "run_id": self.run_id,
            "type": self.type,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "payload": self.payload,
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunContextEntry:
    id: int
    run_id: str
    step: str
    actor: str
    entry_type: str
    timestamp: str
    content: dict[str, Any]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "run_id": self.run_id,
            "step": self.step,
            "actor": self.actor,
            "entry_type": self.entry_type,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "content": self.content,
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunSnapshot:
    run_id: str
    kind: str
    status: RunStatus
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str
    input: dict[str, Any]
    event_count: int
    context: list[dict[str, Any]]
    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    error: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data: dict[str, Any] = {
            "run_id": self.run_id,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "status": self.status,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "updated_at": self.updated_at,
            "input": self.input,
            "event_count": self.event_count,
            "context": self.context,
        }
        if self.result is not None:
            data["result"] = self.result
        if self.error is not None:
            data["error"] = self.error
        return data


@dataclass
class _RunRecord:
    run_id: str
    kind: str
    status: RunStatus
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str
    input: dict[str, Any]
    events: list[RunEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
    context_entries: list[RunContextEntry] = field(default_factory=list)
    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    error: str | None = None

    def snapshot(self) -> RunSnapshot:
        return RunSnapshot(
            run_id=self.run_id,
            kind=self.kind,
            status=self.status,
            created_at=self.created_at,
            updated_at=self.updated_at,
            input=dict(self.input),
            event_count=len(self.events),
            context=[entry.to_dict() for entry in self.context_entries],
            result=self.result,
            error=self.error,
        )


class InMemoryRunStore:
    """Thread-safe run store for the first local-backend vertical slice."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._condition = threading.Condition()
        self._runs: dict[str, _RunRecord] = {}

    def create_run(self, kind: str, input_payload: dict[str, Any]) -> RunSnapshot:
        run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        now = utc_now_iso()
        record = _RunRecord(
            run_id=run_id,
            kind=kind,
            status="queued",
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
            input=dict(input_payload),
        )
        with self._condition:
            self._runs[run_id] = record
            self._append_event_locked(record, "run_created", {"status": record.status})
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return record.snapshot()

    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> RunSnapshot:
        with self._condition:
            return self._record_locked(run_id).snapshot()

    def append_event(self, run_id: str, event_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> RunEvent:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            event = self._append_event_locked(record, event_type, payload)
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return event

    def append_context_entry(
        self,
        run_id: str,
        *,
        step: str,
        actor: str,
        entry_type: str,
        content: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> RunContextEntry:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            now = utc_now_iso()
            record.updated_at = now
            entry = RunContextEntry(
                id=len(record.context_entries) + 1,
                run_id=run_id,
                step=step,
                actor=actor,
                entry_type=entry_type,
                timestamp=now,
                content=dict(content),
            )
            record.context_entries.append(entry)
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return entry

    def context_entries(self, run_id: str) -> list[RunContextEntry]:
        with self._condition:
            return list(self._record_locked(run_id).context_entries)

    def mark_running(self, run_id: str) -> RunSnapshot:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            record.status = "running"
            self._append_event_locked(record, "run_started", {"status": record.status})
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return record.snapshot()

    def mark_succeeded(self, run_id: str, result: dict[str, Any]) -> RunSnapshot:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            record.status = "succeeded"
            record.result = result
            record.error = None
            self._append_event_locked(record, "run_succeeded", {"status": record.status})
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return record.snapshot()

    def update_result(self, run_id: str, result: dict[str, Any]) -> RunSnapshot:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            record.result = result
            record.error = None
            record.updated_at = utc_now_iso()
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return record.snapshot()

    def mark_failed(self, run_id: str, error: str) -> RunSnapshot:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            record.status = "failed"
            record.error = error
            self._append_event_locked(record, "run_failed", {"status": record.status, "error": error})
            self._condition.notify_all()
            return record.snapshot()

    def events_after(self, run_id: str, after_id: int = 0) -> tuple[list[RunEvent], RunSnapshot]:
        with self._condition:
            record = self._record_locked(run_id)
            events = [event for event in record.events if event.id > after_id]
            return events, record.snapshot()

    def wait_for_events_after(
        self,
        run_id: str,
        after_id: int,
        *,
        timeout_seconds: float,
    ) -> tuple[list[RunEvent], RunSnapshot]:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds
        with self._condition:
            while True:
                record = self._record_locked(run_id)
                events = [event for event in record.events if event.id > after_id]
                if events or record.status in TERMINAL_STATUSES:
                    return events, record.snapshot()

                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    return [], record.snapshot()
                self._condition.wait(remaining)

    def wait_for_terminal(self, run_id: str, *, timeout_seconds: float) -> RunSnapshot:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds
        with self._condition:
            while True:
                record = self._record_locked(run_id)
                if record.status in TERMINAL_STATUSES:
                    return record.snapshot()

                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    return record.snapshot()
                self._condition.wait(remaining)

    def _record_locked(self, run_id: str) -> _RunRecord:
        try:
            return self._runs[run_id]
        except KeyError as error:
            raise RunNotFoundError(run_id) from error

    def _append_event_locked(
        self,
        record: _RunRecord,
        event_type: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> RunEvent:
        record.updated_at = utc_now_iso()
        event = RunEvent(
            id=len(record.events) + 1,
            run_id=record.run_id,
            type=event_type,
            timestamp=record.updated_at,
            payload=dict(payload),
        )
        record.events.append(event)
        return event


def format_sse_event(event: RunEvent) -> str:
    data = json.dumps(event.to_dict(), sort_keys=True)
    return f"id: {event.id}\nevent: {event.type}\ndata: {data}\n\n"


def iter_sse_events(
    store: InMemoryRunStore,
    run_id: str,
    *,
    after_id: int = 0,
    wait_timeout_seconds: float = 15.0,
) -> Iterable[str]:
    last_event_id = after_id
    while True:
        events, snapshot = store.events_after(run_id, last_event_id)
        for event in events:
            last_event_id = event.id
            yield format_sse_event(event)

        if snapshot.status in TERMINAL_STATUSES:
            return

        events, snapshot = store.wait_for_events_after(
            run_id,
            last_event_id,
            timeout_seconds=wait_timeout_seconds,
        )
        if not events:
            yield "event: heartbeat\ndata: {}\n\n"

# Vertical Slice Boundaries

## Purpose

Use this document to distinguish workflow slices that prove product behavior in a browser from desktop/product vertical slices that prove the local-first desktop boundary. Issue #19 should use these criteria before treating the current question flow as a repeatable pattern for later workflow stages.

## Current Implemented Slice

The current question flow is a browser-run frontend/backend workflow slice plus a lightweight Tauri shell path around the same app. It proves:

- the Vite/Lit frontend can start a question-clarification run from a browser,
- the frontend can build a temporary CSV profile from the HTML File API,
- the FastAPI backend can run question clarification and question interpretation,
- the frontend can consume backend HTTP endpoints and SSE run events,
- the Tauri shell can wrap the same Vite app in a native window,
- the Tauri shell can discover or start the local FastAPI sidecar,
- the Tauri shell can provide a temporary native CSV/text picker for the same question flow,
- browser-run and desktop-run automated smoke paths can use the same deterministic mock backend contract.

This is not the full product vertical slice for the complete analysis product. It does not yet prove durable project creation, backend-owned ingest, project-folder registration, full pipeline execution, artifact persistence, report generation, report verification, model-assisted repair loops, or export/reproducibility behavior.

## Slice Names

Use these names consistently in docs and issue review:

- Browser-run workflow slice: the Vite/Lit app running through `pnpm dev`, browser unit tests, and browser WebDriver tests against a mocked or developer-started backend.
- Desktop shell slice: the lightweight Tauri wrapper around the existing Vite app, including backend URL discovery, sidecar lifecycle, native file selection, and desktop WebDriver smoke verification.
- Desktop/product vertical slice: an end-to-end user workflow launched from the desktop app that creates or opens a local project, ingests data through product-owned boundaries, runs the relevant backend stages, persists inspectable artifacts, and verifies the user-visible result.

The existing question flow can be called a desktop shell slice after the Tauri smoke path passes. Do not call it a full desktop/product vertical slice without also naming the product behaviors that remain stubbed or temporary.

## Full Desktop/Product Vertical Slice Criteria

A workflow is a full desktop/product vertical slice only when all of these are true:

1. The user starts from the Tauri desktop app, not only from a browser tab.
2. The same workflow remains runnable in the browser-run Vite path for fast frontend development and regression testing.
3. Rust owns only shell responsibilities: startup/shutdown, backend health checks, backend URL discovery, sidecar lifecycle, native file/project selection, app data paths, and OS integration.
4. Product workflow behavior remains in TypeScript and the FastAPI backend.
5. Data ingest crosses a product-owned boundary, produces a durable manifest, and records enough path/hash/type/profile metadata to reproduce the run.
6. The backend owns run state, stage transitions, model calls, tool execution, validation, and persisted snapshots.
7. The workflow writes user-inspectable artifacts into a local project folder or a documented temporary substitute with a clear migration issue.
8. The UI displays live run status from HTTP/SSE contracts and can recover enough state to explain success, failure, or partial results.
9. Automated verification covers unit/build checks, browser-run UI behavior, and desktop-run shell behavior where those paths are touched.
10. Manual verification covers the user-facing desktop path when native dialogs, OS permissions, or packaging behavior cannot be fully automated.

## Acceptable Shortcuts After The Tauri Shell Slice

These shortcuts remain acceptable for the current question-clarification/question-interpretation slice because they keep the Tauri work narrow and preserve the browser-run Vite workflow:

- The TypeScript frontend may still build a temporary CSV profile for the churn fixture before calling the backend run endpoint.
- Browser-run tests may continue to use the HTML File API path and Vite `/api` proxy.
- Desktop tests may use `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_DESKTOP_AUTOMATED_PICK_CSV_PATH` to bypass the real OS picker only in automated WebDriver runs.
- The desktop shell may connect to a mocked backend through `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL` for smoke verification.
- The first Tauri shell may leave installer/signing/bundled-sidecar packaging out of scope.
- The question flow may persist run state in the existing temporary backend store until project-folder persistence is implemented.

## Required Follow-Up Before Reusing The Pattern For Later Stages

Create or resolve focused follow-up issues before later workflow stages copy these shortcuts:

- Move dataset ingest and profiling ownership from the TypeScript temporary profile path to the backend/product ingest boundary.
- Add durable project-folder registration, dataset manifests, file hashes, and artifact path rules.
- Persist run state and stage snapshots outside the in-memory slice store.
- Define the backend contracts for feasibility, analysis execution, evidence manifests, report generation, and report verification before building matching UI states.
- Decide which desktop file/project permissions are needed for real project folders instead of a single temporary CSV/text picker.
- Expand desktop verification when native packaging, app data directories, updater behavior, or OS file reveal/open actions are implemented.

## Issue #19 Review Inputs

Before issue #19 resumes, reviewers should treat issue #32 and its child issues as the evidence for the desktop shell boundary. The review question is not whether the question workflow is complete product behavior. It is whether the split among Rust shell, TypeScript frontend, FastAPI backend, model service, browser-run tests, and desktop-run tests is clear enough to repeat safely.

The minimum review inputs are:

- [system-architecture.md](system-architecture.md) for long-term component ownership,
- [desktop-shell.md](desktop-shell.md) for current Tauri responsibilities and browser-run preservation rules,
- this document for slice naming, product-slice criteria, and accepted shortcuts,
- [../testing/frontend-browser-ui.md](../testing/frontend-browser-ui.md) and [../testing/desktop-tauri-smoke.md](../testing/desktop-tauri-smoke.md) for verification expectations.

# Desktop Shell

## Status

Accepted for the first Tauri v2 desktop shell scaffold.

## Purpose

`apps/desktop` is still the TypeScript Vite/Lit frontend source of truth. The Tauri shell wraps that existing app in a native desktop window and should stay limited to shell responsibilities. Product workflow behavior remains in TypeScript and the local FastAPI backend.

This document describes the desktop shell slice, not the full desktop/product vertical slice. The browser-run workflow slice, desktop shell slice, and product vertical-slice criteria are defined in [vertical-slice-boundaries.md](vertical-slice-boundaries.md).

## Project Structure

```text
apps/desktop/
  package.json
  vite.config.ts
  src/
  src-tauri/
    Cargo.toml
    build.rs
    tauri.conf.json
    src/backend_sidecar.rs
    src/main.rs
```

`src-tauri/src/main.rs` should remain a thin `tauri::Builder` bootstrap plus shell-only native capabilities. The current native surface is limited to local FastAPI sidecar lifecycle management, `GET /health` readiness checks, `get_backend_url()`, which lets the shell tell the frontend where the local backend is running, and `pick_csv_file()`, which is a temporary desktop-only CSV/text file picker and safe file-read handoff for the first question flow. Do not move question clarification, question interpretation, dataset profiling, SSE handling, model configuration, durable project ingest, or backend API workflow logic into Rust.

## Browser-Run Workflow

The browser-run frontend path remains supported and is the default path for automated frontend work:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
pnpm dev
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:ui
```

Vite still serves the browser app on `127.0.0.1:5173` by default and proxies `/api` to `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL`, falling back to `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The browser UI test harness starts Vite on its own available port and points it at a mocked backend, so those tests do not require Tauri, FastAPI, or a live model endpoint.

Browser builds and browser-run tests keep using `/api` so the Vite proxy remains the only browser backend-discovery mechanism. Frontend API helpers must not read desktop-only assumptions when the Tauri runtime globals are absent.

## Tauri Workflow

The desktop shell uses the same Vite app:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
pnpm run tauri:dev
```

For this repository's default desktop development setup, `pnpm run tauri:dev` points the backend sidecar at the documented remote LAN/VPN model server. To force the same-machine LLM default at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`, use:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
pnpm run tauri:dev:local-llm
```

The Tauri config runs `scripts/with-node.sh vite` before desktop development and loads `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. Production desktop builds run the existing frontend build through the same Node/Corepack wrapper first and embed `../dist`:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
pnpm run tauri:build
```

Desktop development launches through `apps/desktop/scripts/tauri-dev.sh`. On
the local Hyprland/NVIDIA development host, WebKitGTK can exit with
`Gdk-Message: Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display` when
the WebKit DMABUF renderer is enabled. The wrapper keeps native Wayland as the
default display path and disables that renderer:

```text
GDK_BACKEND=${GDK_BACKEND:-wayland,x11}
WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1
```

To force XWayland or retest the DMABUF path, override the wrapper-specific
variables:

```bash
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_TAURI_GDK_BACKEND=x11 pnpm run tauri:dev:local-llm
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0 pnpm run tauri:dev:local-llm
```

Bundling is currently disabled in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` because the current slice only proves a local development shell around the existing frontend and Python backend. Later signing, installer, and bundled sidecar work should enable only the bundle targets needed by that issue.

When the frontend first asks for the backend URL, the shell checks `GET /health` at `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL` when that variable is set. If the configured backend is healthy, the shell connects to it and does not spawn a process. If `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL` is set but unhealthy, the shell reports that configured backend failure to the frontend instead of silently starting a different backend.

When `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL` is not set, the shell checks the default backend at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. If no healthy backend is already running there, Tauri starts the local FastAPI sidecar with:

```bash
apps/backend/.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn insight_specialist_backend.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

If `apps/backend/.venv/bin/python` does not exist, the shell falls back to `python3`. Override the Python executable with `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_PYTHON` and the backend working directory with `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_DIR` when testing alternate local environments. The shell sets `PYTHONPATH` to the backend `src` directory and otherwise inherits the backend environment, including `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_BASE_URL`, `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_MODEL`, and `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_LLM_API_KEY`. Model-server configuration remains owned by the backend process.

The shell waits for `GET /health` before `get_backend_url()` succeeds. This backend discovery is initialized lazily so native setup does not block the WebView event loop, but the current frontend calls it as soon as the root app connects. If readiness fails, the frontend shows the returned desktop error state before the user starts a run. The managed Tauri state kills only the sidecar process it started when the desktop app exits; it leaves externally started or `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_BACKEND_URL` configured backend processes alone. Cleanup is triggered explicitly from Tauri window-close and app-exit events, with the managed-state destructor kept as a fallback.

In the desktop runtime, the frontend discovers the backend through the shell command `get_backend_url()`. TypeScript owns URL construction after discovery: relative backend paths such as `/runs/{run_id}` and `/runs/{run_id}/events` are joined to the discovered backend URL in Tauri, while the same paths are joined to `/api` in browser/dev mode. This keeps backend URL discovery a shell responsibility and keeps product workflow logic in the TypeScript app and FastAPI backend.

The desktop runtime also exposes `pick_csv_file()` for the temporary CSV question flow. The command opens a native file picker filtered to `.csv` and `.txt`, rejects unsupported extensions and files larger than 10 MB, reads UTF-8 text, and returns only the file name, size, path, and text needed by the TypeScript frontend. The picker must use the non-blocking dialog API so the Tauri WebView remains responsive while the OS dialog is open. For automated desktop WebDriver tests only, `INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_DESKTOP_AUTOMATED_PICK_CSV_PATH` can point the command at a deterministic CSV fixture instead of opening the OS dialog. The frontend then builds the same temporary CSV profile used by the browser-run file input path. This is an acceptable desktop shell shortcut for the current question flow, but it is not final backend-owned ingest, project-folder registration, or durable data persistence.

For WebView debugging, Tauri dev/debug builds expose the platform inspector. Use right-click `Inspect Element`, `Ctrl+Shift+I` on Linux or Windows, or `Command+Option+I` on macOS. If input focus or event handling is broken and shortcuts cannot be trusted, start the debug shell with:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
INSIGHT_SPECIALIST_DESKTOP_OPEN_DEVTOOLS=1 pnpm run tauri:dev
```

The shell opens devtools programmatically during Tauri setup only in Rust debug builds. This is a local debugging aid and should not be treated as production inspector support.

## Local Prerequisites

Desktop shell work requires:

- the app's pinned Node/pnpm workflow,
- Rust and Cargo,
- the Tauri v2 system dependencies for the developer's operating system.
- the local backend Python environment when Tauri should start the sidecar:

```bash
python -m venv apps/backend/.venv
apps/backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e apps/backend
```

On Linux, Tauri requires WebKitGTK 4.1 and related build libraries. On macOS, install Xcode or Xcode Command Line Tools. On Windows, install Microsoft C++ Build Tools and WebView2. Use the official Tauri prerequisites page when setting up a new workstation because package names vary by OS and distribution: <https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/>.

## Verification

For shell changes, follow [../engineering/verification/tauri-shell.md](../engineering/verification/tauri-shell.md). The core deterministic checks for scaffold changes are:

```bash
cd apps/desktop
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:ui
pnpm run test:desktop
cd src-tauri
cargo check
cargo test
```

When backend URL discovery changes, `pnpm test` must cover both browser `/api` URL construction and Tauri command-based URL construction. Browser UI tests must continue to run through the mocked backend and Vite proxy.

Manual desktop verification for the workflow slice is:

1. Start `pnpm run test:desktop` from `apps/desktop`.
2. Confirm the automated WebDriver pass drives backend discovery, desktop file selection, SSE progress, clarification answers, and `churn_driver_analysis` interpretation.

Manual WebView devtools verification is:

class FakeModelClient:
    def __init__(self, *response_contents: str) -> None:
        self.response_contents = list(response_contents)
        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def chat_completion(
        self,
        messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        *,
        temperature: float | None = None,
        max_tokens: int | None = None,
    ) -> ChatResult:
        self.calls.append(

class RunStoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_run_store_records_events_and_terminal_result(self) -> None:
        store = InMemoryRunStore()
        snapshot = store.create_run("test_run", {"raw_question": "Why?"})

        self.assertEqual(snapshot.status, "queued")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot.event_count, 1)

        store.mark_running(snapshot.run_id)
        store.append_event(snapshot.run_id, "stage_started", {"stage": "question_clarification"})
        finished = store.mark_succeeded(snapshot.run_id, {"answer": 42})

        self.assertEqual(finished.status, "succeeded")
        self.assertEqual(finished.result, {"answer": 42})
        events, _ = store.events_after(snapshot.run_id)
        self.assertEqual(
            [event.type for event in events],
            ["run_created", "run_started", "stage_started", "run_succeeded"],
        )

    def test_run_store_records_context_entries(self) -> None:
        store = InMemoryRunStore()
        snapshot = store.create_run("test_run", {"raw_question": "Why?"})

        entry = store.append_context_entry(
            snapshot.run_id,
            step="define_question",
            actor="user",
            entry_type="analysis_request",
            content={"raw_question": "Why?"},
        )

        self.assertEqual(entry.id, 1)
        updated = store.get_run(snapshot.run_id)
        self.assertEqual(updated.context[0]["step"], "define_question")
        self.assertEqual(updated.context[0]["content"]["raw_question"], "Why?")

    def test_sse_format_uses_event_id_type_and_json_payload(self) -> None:
        store = InMemoryRunStore()
        snapshot = store.create_run("test_run", {"raw_question": "Why?"})
        event = store.append_event(snapshot.run_id, "stage_started", {"stage": "question_clarification"})

        formatted = format_sse_event(event)

        self.assertIn(f"id: {event.id}\n", formatted)
        self.assertIn("event: stage_started\n", formatted)
        self.assertTrue(formatted.endswith("\n\n"))
        data_line = next(line for line in formatted.splitlines() if line.startswith("data: "))
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(data_line.removeprefix("data: "))["type"], "stage_started")

    def test_sse_iterator_replays_existing_events_and_closes_after_terminal_event(self) -> None:
        store = InMemoryRunStore()
        snapshot = store.create_run("test_run", {"raw_question": "Why?"})
        store.mark_succeeded(snapshot.run_id, {"answer": 42})

        chunks = list(iter_sse_events(store, snapshot.run_id))

        self.assertEqual(len(chunks), 2)
        self.assertIn("event: run_created", chunks[0])
        self.assertIn("event: run_succeeded", chunks[1])

# Durable local question-run boundary (proposal, not implemented)

## Decision and scope

Make FastAPI + a local SQLite database the authority for question-clarification **and its optional question-interpretation continuation**. Lit owns presentation and a disposable connection; Rust owns backend discovery, local app-data path provisioning, and sidecar lifecycle, not workflow state. Preserve browser/Vite `/api` and Tauri `get_backend_url` paths. No hosted service, account, cloud credential, or remote production dependency is assumed. The model endpoint may be unavailable; restoration must work without contacting it. This is a run-state boundary, **not** durable dataset ingest or a project-folder implementation. The temporary frontend CSV profile is still the input; record that limitation and do not promise reproducibility from the original file.

### Findings in the current slice

- `apps/desktop/src/api/insight-specialist-api.ts` posts `/runs/question-clarification`, fetches `/runs/{id}`, posts answers and resolves relative URLs through Vite `/api` or the Tauri-discovered backend. It accepts absolute URLs, has no response validation or durable run pointer, and reports network failures as errors.
- `apps/backend/src/insight_specialist_backend/main.py` returns a queued snapshot with `run_id`, `run_url`, `events_url`; GET snapshot and SSE with `?after`/`Last-Event-ID` already exist. `runs.py` allocates random UUID-hex run IDs and per-run integer event/context IDs, but retains everything in a process-local `InMemoryRunStore`. Events and results are not transactional. `question_clarification_runs.py` runs daemon threads, marks clarification `succeeded` even if answers are required, then moves that same run from `succeeded` back to `running` on answers; it does not reject duplicate or concurrent answer submissions. A backend restart loses both history and running work.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/insight-specialist-app/insight-specialist-app.ts` keeps `run`, `snapshot`, `events`, profile, file name, selected step, and captured answers only in Lit state. It fetches snapshots only on terminal SSE, derives the answer replay cursor from `snapshot.event_count ?? events.length`, appends replay events without dedupe, closes SSE on every `run_succeeded`, and treats failed POST/SSE/snapshot reads as run failures. `clarification-step` hides the form based on client-only captured answers. Reload/restart therefore loses the run even if the backend survives. `backend_sidecar.rs` kills only a Tauri-spawned backend on desktop exit, so backend persistence alone cannot keep an in-flight daemon thread alive through an ordinary desktop restart.

## Ownership alternatives

| Choice | Benefits | Costs / restart behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop-owned state (Lit/localStorage or Rust-side store), replay/request stages after restart | Fast UI-only prototype; survives WebView reload | Copies sensitive input/results into a second store; cannot authoritatively know whether a model call completed; duplicate POSTs and diverging event IDs; Rust would acquire product workflow responsibility. Not sufficient for sidecar termination. |
| Backend-owned SQLite snapshot + event/context log; UI stores only a locator hint (**recommended**) | One source of truth for commands, progress, results, and recovery; HTTP/SSE contract shared by browser and Tauri; no model calls needed to read old runs | Requires migrations, transactional writes, interrupted-work policy, app-data path and same-store discovery. Running work does not magically resume after sidecar death. |
| Keep a persistent backend daemon while Tauri exits | An actual in-flight model call may finish without interruption | Process supervision, upgrade, cleanup and ownership become a separate product feature; not reliable across machine reboot. Defer; supported as a developer-managed backend today. |

## Identity, storage and API contract

1. Provision a stable per-user app-data directory and SQLite DB for the backend, independent of checkout and current working directory (browser-run development gets an explicit local DB path override, tests use temporary DBs). Rust passes the resolved path to its spawned backend; an externally managed backend advertises its own store identity. Do not send the DB path to the WebView. Enable WAL, busy timeout, foreign keys, schema-version migrations, atomic transactions and a single local worker owner; reject unsupported newer schemas rather than recreating them. Restrict file permissions to the local user and keep raw question, dataset profile, answers, context and model output out of URL/query strings and diagnostics. Loopback binding/CORS is not authentication: retain narrow origins and avoid arbitrary absolute backend-provided URLs.
2. Add opaque `store_id` (stable UUID generated in DB) and schema/contract version to `/health` or a small local capabilities endpoint. `run_id` remains a backend-generated opaque UUID (existing hex IDs remain valid inside the same store). Event IDs are monotonically increasing integers **per run**, never reset, including across clarification and interpretation; context IDs likewise. Snapshot `event_count` becomes the last committed event ID (for a contiguous log it is also the count). `run_id` plus `store_id` is the locator; do not confuse a new process on the same port with the same store. Return only relative `run_url`/`events_url`; frontend constructs paths from validated IDs on the current discovered backend, not from arbitrary absolute URLs.
3. Persist `runs` (kind, status, current_stage, timestamps, input, result, structured error, revision), `run_events` (run_id, sequence, timestamp, type, payload) and `run_context` (run_id, sequence, actor, step, type, content) in a transaction for each accepted command/transition. All readers see a committed snapshot and ordered events. Treat SSE as a replayable notification stream, **GET snapshot as authoritative**. Keep existing `POST /runs/question-clarification`, `GET /runs/{id}`, `GET /runs/{id}/events?after=N`, `POST /runs/{id}/clarification-answers`; add `GET /runs?kind=question_clarification` (bounded newest-first summaries with pagination) to recover if the UI locator is missing. Do not return full dataset profiles in list rows. Return a stable `store_id` on snapshots/list replies, and version contracts before rollout.
4. On create, accept a client-generated `request_id` (UUID, scoped to store) as an idempotency key; enforce unique key and request-body digest. Same key+body returns the same run/URLs, mismatched body returns 409. Persist the request ID on the client **before** POST, keep it after a timeout, query by request ID (or retry same POST) before offering a new run. Backend creates the queued run, analysis_request context and `run_created` event atomically before returning 202; dispatch happens after commit. For answers accept `command_id` similarly scoped to run; same command/body returns current snapshot without appending context or starting another worker; conflicting body returns 409. Validation errors are 400/422 without mutation. Require a persisted `awaiting_clarification` revision on answer submission (optimistic revision/unique accepted-answers command) so parallel different submissions cannot both start interpretation.
5. UI may persist a small locator `{store_id, run_id, request_id?, last_seen_event_id?}` in browser localStorage/Tauri WebView storage, never a copy of the profile or answers. If browser storage is cleared, list runs and allow the user to select one; on wrong store, show an explicit backend mismatch and allow choosing this backend's runs without deleting the old locator. Do not select a run solely because its ID matches across stores. Expose a stable manual way to reopen an older run. Avoid overwriting an unacknowledged create request's key with a new one until reconciliation completes.

## State machine and reconnection

- New runs: `queued -> running` (clarification). Clarification success with blocking questions: `running -> awaiting_clarification` with spec/result persisted, and a `run_awaiting_clarification` event; no blockers: `running -> succeeded` (clarification-only slice). Do not automatically infer interpretation for no-blocker runs until product behavior explicitly specifies that transition. A valid accepted answer command: `awaiting_clarification -> running` (interpretation) with answers in result/context and an event; then `running -> succeeded` with interpretation result, or `running -> failed` with stage-scoped error. Stage result survives later interpretation failure. `failed`, `succeeded`, `interrupted` are terminal for this run; no `succeeded -> running`. If later stages need a continuation after completion, create a linked new run rather than reopening a terminal run. SSE ends at terminal **or waiting-for-user**; answer POST starts a new stream segment with the same event sequence.
- Sidecar shutdown/restart: persist a worker generation/lease and stage before dispatch. On startup, convert stale `queued`/`running` work owned by a dead generation to `interrupted` with a durable `run_interrupted` event and safe diagnostic code; do not automatically replay a non-idempotent model call or assert it succeeded. Explicit "retry as new run" copies the stored question/profile and links `parent_run_id`, after user confirmation; preserve original log. If the backend stays alive while only the window restarts, the same run continues normally. Treat failed/interrupted separately in UI. A live but temporarily disconnected backend is **not** an interrupted run.
- Startup/reconnect: discover/health-check backend; compare `store_id`; resolve pending create key first, otherwise GET saved run, or list if no locator. Hydrate question, temporary profile, current_stage, spec, accepted answers (from backend result/context), interpretation, status and error from snapshot. File name is not in the current request: either persist a safe display-only original filename on create or show "Previously selected data" on restored runs, never a fabricated path. Derive wizard step from current_stage and result, not the latest SSE alone. Render immediately from snapshot, then subscribe `?after=<last seen per-run event ID>`; if no cached events, replay from 0 (bounded/page history for large runs). Dedupe by `(store_id, run_id, event.id)`, sort by ID and detect gaps; on gap or stream error refetch snapshot and reconnect with bounded backoff, including when the stream ends without a terminal snapshot. Refetch after answer acknowledgement and after terminal/waiting events. No heartbeat is stored or counted. Never use `events.length` as cursor. On reconnect, restore only acknowledged answers; preserve drafts locally only if explicitly designed for privacy.
- HTTP/network errors are not workflow failures. Show "backend unavailable, retrying" and keep the last snapshot; retry discovery, clear a rejected backend URL cache, and revalidate store identity. 404 after matching store -> run missing/deleted, offer list/new run; 409 -> refetch authoritative snapshot and explain stale/duplicate action; schema-too-new/corrupt DB -> visible actionable error, no silent reset. An SSE disconnect never changes durable status to `failed`. Sanitize persisted model exception text in public errors: stable code, stage, retryability and safe message; detailed trace only in local restricted logs. If create/answer acknowledgement is lost, reconcile idempotency key before retrying; disable the command button while pending.

## Delivery, migration, rollback

1. Add DB schema/repository behind the run-store interface and transaction tests; wire backend to a configured local app-data path. Keep an ephemeral store only as an explicit test/dev mode. Add `store_id`, new statuses, stage and idempotency to API types and a documented contract. Preserve old paths and SSE event shapes where possible; update `run_succeeded` meaning only after the UI understands `awaiting_clarification`.
2. Add read/list/recovery and crash marking before switching the UI. Update mocks and browser/Tauri startup so tests never share a real user's DB. Then update UI hydration, locator, cursor, reconnect and answer controls. Finally remove the old terminal-reopen behavior. Gate rollout on a version/capabilities check rather than guessing from status fields.
3. Existing in-memory runs cannot be imported across a killed backend; acknowledge loss and prompt a new run. For a live legacy process, continue its existing contract until replaced, then report those runs unavailable. Persisted DB migrations are versioned, forward-only with a backup before upgrade; on upgrade failure leave original DB intact, expose failure and do not fall back to an empty store. No automatic import of browser local state beyond a validated locator. Never place DB in the git checkout.
4. Rollback: keep the previous build and pre-migration DB backup; stop sidecar before restoring both together. An older backend must refuse a newer schema rather than overwrite it. A frontend-only rollback may read old contracts if explicitly supported, but cannot safely post answers across the changed state machine; disable writes on contract mismatch. Preserve the DB and export diagnostics/backup before any destructive reset. Remove feature flag only after recovery tests pass.

## Verification / acceptance criteria (to implement, not claimed passing)

- Backend tests (`apps/backend/tests/unit/test_runs.py` and API integration with temp SQLite, fake model, no live LLM): process recreation recovers queued/waiting/succeeded/failed/interrupted snapshots and exact context/events; stale running becomes interrupted; same `run_id`/event cursor survive restart; concurrent answer commands yield one interpretation; same/different idempotency key payloads and validation failures have no duplicate effects; failed interpretation retains clarification; SSE `after` replay, heartbeat, closure at waiting/terminal, cursor beyond latest, missing/deleted run; schema upgrade/backup/unsupported version and DB I/O errors; safe public error serialization and data isolation.
- Frontend unit tests for browser `/api` and Tauri-discovered URL, store mismatch, 404/409/offline, lost POST acknowledgement, deduped/gapped SSE and snapshot-as-authority. Browser UI mock tests: reload while running, after clarification prompts, while interpretation runs, after success/failure, and offline/reconnect; answer exactly once and restore captured answers/step. Tauri WebDriver smoke: close/relaunch Tauri-managed sidecar while model call is blocked -> interrupted with old log visible; externally managed backend/window-only restart -> run remains active/completes. Use mock/fake backend, no cloud or live model required.
- Manual desktop check: start with a temporary DB and fixture CSV, close/relaunch at each state, confirm correct run/store and accurate file label, resume SSE or see interruption, then answer/reopen terminal result; verify alternate configured local backend does not silently show another store's run. Run the domain checks in `docs/authoritative/engineering/verification/{backend,desktop-frontend,tauri-shell}.md` when implementing. Do not call this full desktop/product vertical slice until backend-owned ingest and project artifact persistence exist.
